inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted count for Q3 2026 (10-Q EPS note: basic 3,240m + 301m dilutive stock-based awards, which includes the ~286.5m restricted shares issued on net exercise of the 2018 CEO Performance Award). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. EXCLUDES the 423.7m unearned restricted shares of the 2025 CEO Performance Award, which are in the 3,953m 'issued and outstanding' balance-sheet figure but vest only on market-cap milestones of $2.0T-$8.5T plus operational milestones; their cost is carried through the SBC path (heavier in the bull case), not through the divisor. If every tranche were earned the count would be ~12% higher.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement add-back, TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 2,825 + 9M-2026 3,346 - 9M-2025 1,871 (10-K FY2025, 10-Q Q3 2026). Tesla publishes no combined figure and reports no separate cash-tax-on-net-settlement line (awards are sell-to-cover), so nothing is added. TTM includes ~1.07bn/yr run-rate for the 2025 CEO Performance Award (275m in Q3 2026).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 11.5% in all three scenarios = 9.5% base + 2.0% of explicit structural premia added in the 2026-11-15 sanity-check fix pass. BASE 9.5%: risk-free ~4.2% (10-yr UST) + ~5% ERP x beta ~1.05; no debt tilt because the company is net cash and its 9.3bn of debt is non-recourse ABS. PREMIUM 1, extreme cyclicality, +1.0% (low end of the 1.0-2.0% band): GAAP operating income fell from 13.7bn (16.8% margin, FY2022) to a 3.5bn TTM pace (3.3%), roughly 4x peak-to-trough in three years on price cuts and falling deliveries, and owner FCF went from +5.7bn to -2.7bn; a 1.05 beta does not describe that earnings stream. PREMIUM 2, regulatory single point of failure, +1.0% (low end of the 1.0-2.0% band): the margin recovery in the base and bull paths depends on regulators permitting unsupervised driving at scale, jurisdiction by jurisdiction, and an adverse NHTSA/state ruling or a serious-incident suspension would stop the Robotaxi/FSD revenue that carries those paths. NOT ADDED: a key-person premium for the CEO; it is real, but it is the same exposure as the autonomy pivot and is carried by the 25% bear weight, and stacking it would take the rate toward the ~14% a raw-beta CAPM gives. Both premia are taken at the low end because the scenario spread and weights already carry part of this dispersion; the rate now charges the part of it that is not diversifiable across scenarios (every scenario shares the cyclical auto base and the regulatory gate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases left inside EBITDA as rent (US GAAP, straight-line in opex); operating lease liabilities NOT in net debt. Finance leases (256m) are inside total_debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; noncontrolling interests (546m) and redeemable NCI (54m) deducted at book in the equity bridge. NCI income is ~60m/yr, immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; US filer, no adaptations needed), 10-year horizon because margins and capex are far from mature. Robotaxi/FSD, energy storage and Optimus are NOT valued as separate option add-ons: they are inside the revenue-growth and margin paths of each scenario, so the bear/base/bull spread IS the optionality. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet ends (using FY2025 as FY0 would re-count 9 months of cash already in the Sep-30 cash balance). TTM: revenue 103,570; operating income 3,466 (3.3%); D&A 6,704; SBC 4,300; adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC) 14,470 = 14.0%; OCF 18,710; capex 15,407 (2026 guided 'in excess of $20 billion'); reported FCF 3,303; owner FCF -2,747 after SBC and 1,750 of interest income (stripped because 35.9bn of net cash is added in the bridge). Tesla does not repurchase stock: the flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for; basic shares have drifted up ~0.4%/yr. PRICE: regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Scenario flag: none of the three scenarios hits the zero terminal floor. Cash includes 27.6bn short-term investments; restricted cash (1,153m) excluded. Three undrawn credit agreements of $30bn were signed September 2026 - management is signalling capex beyond operating cash flow.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: 10-yr base revenue path averaging ~12.6%/yr; equity CAGR rejected as an anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (22.1%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (5.2%) and EPS (-33.2%). Book value has compounded on retained earnings, a 5.0bn FY2023 deferred-tax valuation-allowance release and SBC credited to paid-in capital while revenue stalled and earnings fell by two-thirds from the FY2022 peak. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020, fiscal years. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 1,022; FY2022 5,709; FY2025 1,715; TTM Sep-2026 -2,747. Owner-FCF CAGRs sit well below reported (3-yr -33.0% vs -6.3%; 5-yr 10.9% vs 17.4%): SBC has grown from 1.56bn (FY2022) to a 4.3bn TTM pace and interest income from 0.3bn to 1.75bn, so a rising share of reported FCF is either paid for in stock or earned by the cash pile rather than the operations.

base.narrative: Revenue ~3.3x to ~$340bn in ten years; GAAP operating margin recovers from 3.3% to ~17.4% (above the FY2022 peak of 16.8%) on autonomy and energy mix.

bull.narrative: Revenue ~7.6x to ~$790bn; GAAP operating margin ~27% on a robotaxi/FSD/Optimus-led mix. SBC runs heavier because further 2025 CEO Performance Award milestones become probable.

bear.narrative: Revenue ~1.4x to ~$150bn; GAAP operating margin ~5%, an ordinary automaker-plus-storage business carrying a compute build that never earns its cost. Cap multiple 12x for a cyclical manufacturer.

scenario_narratives.base: Autonomy works, but as a business that scales over a decade rather than a switch that flips. The Robotaxi service (launched June 2025) and Cybercab (September 2026) expand city by city; FSD take-rates and Services & other (already +41% in 9M-2026, 16.3bn TTM) carry growth while vehicle deliveries grow in the mid-single digits from a ~1.8m/yr pace and regulatory credits (639m in 9M-2026, down 56%) fade to nothing. Energy storage resumes growth after a flat 2026 (36 GWh deployed in nine months, revenue -6% on pricing and tariff refunds). Revenue reaches ~$340bn by year 10 and the GAAP operating margin climbs from 3.3% to ~17%, slightly above the FY2022 peak, because high-margin software and ride revenue offsets a structurally lower auto margin. Capex stays at ~20% of revenue through 2027 for compute, Cybercab, Semi, cell, semiconductor and Optimus lines, then falls toward 7.5%; owner FCF is negative for the first two years and matures at ~13% of revenue. Optimus is in the R&D line, not the revenue line.
scenario_narratives.bull: Unsupervised autonomy generalises quickly: a company-operated and owner-contributed robotaxi fleet in the millions, FSD licensed or sold at high attach rates worldwide, and Optimus reaching commercial volume late in the decade, alongside storage growing with data-centre and grid demand. Revenue compounds ~22%/yr to ~$790bn with pre-SBC EBITDA margin of 38%. This is the path the 2025 CEO Performance Award is written for (1 million Robotaxis in commercial operation is one of its milestones), so SBC is charged at 5-6% of revenue in the middle years as further tranches become probable (the 10-Q carries $106-120bn of unrecognised expense on milestones not yet deemed probable), and capex stays above 10% of revenue for eight years. It needs regulatory approval, a safety record, fleet economics and a second product category all to land.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tesla remains what the last three years of numbers describe: deliveries fell in 2024 and 2025, automotive revenue is below FY2023, operating margin has gone from 16.8% to 3.3%, and Chinese and legacy EV competition keeps pricing pressure on. In this path Robotaxi stays geofenced and sub-scale against Waymo and Chinese operators, FSD faces regulatory and litigation limits, credits disappear, storage commoditises, and the >$20bn/yr AI and factory build is cut back only after two years of negative free cash flow. Revenue grows 2-5%/yr to ~$150bn with a ~5% operating margin. Value is then little more than today's net cash plus a low-multiple manufacturer; the scenario does not hit the zero terminal floor, but most of its per-share value is the balance sheet.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the thesis rests on a pivot (autonomy, robots) that is launched but commercially unproven, while the core auto business has shrunk for two years and owner FCF is negative. Base 50%: it already assumes autonomy succeeds enough to lift margins above the prior peak. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once - regulatory clearance for unsupervised driving at scale, robotaxi unit economics, and Optimus commercialisation - and competitors are not standing still.

The closest analogs are not usable as caps: the 10-yr P/E range is 38.8x-338.6x (avg 179.3x) and P/Sales 0.18x-24.2x (avg 9.5x), all far above what the model capitalises at. At 11.5% WACC and 3% growth the Gordon terminal is 12.1x year-10 owner FCF in base and bull (bear binds at its 12x cap), i.e. below every historical multiple, so a history-derived cap would never bind.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tesla is valued as one operating company on strict owner free cash flow, with the autonomy, energy and robotics optionality expressed as scenario paths rather than bolted-on option values. The starting point is uncomfortable and should be read first: trailing owner FCF is negative (-2.7bn) once 4.3bn of SBC and 1.75bn of interest on the cash pile are removed, operating margin is 3.3%, and capex is running above $20bn a year. Everything above net cash plus a modest manufacturer is therefore payment for businesses that barely show in today's revenue. The base case grants a great deal - revenue more than tripling and margins exceeding the prior peak - and still lands far below the market price; the price is only reached on something close to the bull path, held with certainty. Terminal value is ~75% of enterprise value in the base and bull cases and more than all of it in the bear case (interim flows net to slightly negative), so these numbers are sensitive to the year-10 margin and the discount rate above all. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-11-15): the first build (9.5% WACC, weighted IV 158.09) tripped the multiples check on implied P/E alone - 417.9x against a gate of 2x the 10-yr average of 179.3x - while implied P/B (5.2x vs avg 13.9x) and P/Sales (4.5x vs avg 9.5x) sat far below history. Much of that P/E is a denominator effect: SBC-adjusted trailing EPS is a few tens of cents at a 3.3% operating margin, so almost any positive value for the franchise reads as hundreds of times earnings. The part that was a genuine model issue is that a 9.5% rate built on a 1.05 beta treated a business whose operating income has fallen ~4x in three years, and whose recovery depends on a regulatory permission it does not control, as an average-risk equity. The one-pass fix adds +1.0% for cyclicality and +1.0% for the regulatory gate, taking WACC to 11.5% in every scenario; growth, margin, capex and weights were left alone. Result: bear 16.42, base 81.46, bull 266.62, weighted 111.49. THESIS FRAMING: the market price is a payment for multi-bagger optionality (robotaxi, FSD licensing, Optimus) held with near-certainty; even the bull path, discounted at a rate that charges for the cyclical base and the regulatory gate, is worth about two-thirds of the price. This is not a statement that the optionality is worthless - it is the bull case and it is worth more than three times the base - but that an owner paying today's price is underwriting the bull path plus a discount rate below 10%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-heavy: interim owner FCF is negative to thin for years, so nearly all value sits in a year-10 margin that no current segment earns
Upside the model may understate: Optimus is not in base revenue at all, and a faster robotaxi ramp than the bull path is what the market price implies
Dilution outside the divisor: 423.7m unearned 2025 CEO award shares (~12%) vest only at $2.0T-$8.5T market cap; charged via SBC, with $106-120bn of expense not yet deemed probable
Capex and funding: >$20bn capex in 2026 against ~$19bn TTM operating cash flow, and $30bn of new credit lines signed September 2026
Related-party capital allocation: $2.0bn SpaceX (ex-xAI) equity purchase in 2026 and Megapack sales to SpaceX
Regulatory credits, tariffs and IRA/OBBBA credit changes move auto and storage margins by amounts comparable to current operating income
Operating cash flow is flattered by payables: accounts payable and accruals contributed 7.3bn in 9M-2026
